prs.title: fix: Round vault share conversions in the vault's favor (fixCleanup3_6_0)
prs.author: muhammadsalah

comments.author: muhammadsalah

prs.body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Supersedes #7824, which was closed and can't be reopened. The earlier review discussion is there.

Under the `fixCleanup3_6_0` amendment, the vault's share/asset conversions for XRP and MPT vaults are computed exactly and rounded in the vault's favor, so a single depositor or withdrawer can no longer dilute the other shareholders through round-to-nearest:

- **Deposit**: the shares minted round down and the assets charged for them round up, so the depositor pays at least the fair value of the shares.
- **Withdraw**: the shares burned (withdraw by amount) round down and the assets paid for them round down, so the withdrawer receives at most the fair value of the shares.

### Context of Change

The conversions computed `assetsTotal * shares / sharesTotal` in `Number` and quantized to the asset with round-to-nearest. On a vault holding an integral asset at a non-unit share price:

- a deposit could be charged up to half a unit less than the shares are worth, and
- a withdrawal could be paid up to half a unit more than the shares are worth.

Either way, the remaining shareholders cover the difference.

Rounding each `Number` step up or down is not enough. `Number` keeps 19 digits, so with large totals a directed rounding mode can move an exact result by a whole unit. With `AssetsTotal = SharesTotal = 1,000,000,000,000,007` (price exactly 1), a deposit of 123,456,789 has to charge 123,456,789, but `AssetsTotal * shares` needs 24 digits, and rounding up at every step charges 123,456,790. The deposit then fails with `tecINTERNAL` ("would take more than offered"). For XRP and MPT every operand is an integer, so the conversions now compute `a * b / c` in 128 bits and round once.

Changes, all behind `fixCleanup3_6_0` (`fixCleanup3_5_0` is already in 3.5.0-rc1):

- The four conversion helpers take a `VaultRounding` argument (`Legacy` by default). `FavorVault` uses the exact integer path for XRP and MPT. IOU conversions keep the existing arithmetic, since an IOU result is not exact anyway and the `fixCleanup3_4_0` scale clamps already round IOU amounts in the vault's favor.
- `VaultWithdraw` truncates the withdraw-by-amount share count under the new gate too, so it no longer depends on `fixCleanup3_4_0` being enabled.
- When a share is worth less than one unit, a non-final `VaultWithdraw` whose rounded-down payout is zero, while the vault still has withdrawable value, fails with `tecPRECISION_LOSS` instead of burning shares for nothing. The final withdrawal is unaffected.
- `VaultWithdraw::preclaim` uses the same rounding so the withdrawal-limit check estimates the amount `doApply` will pay.
- Clawback is unchanged.

These address findings from [Common Prefix](https://www.commonprefix.com/)'s public formal verification of the XRPL vault and lending protocol ([`testVaultDepositOvervaluedShares`](https://github.com/commonprefix/rippled-formal-verification/blob/lending-protocol-fv/src/test/formal_verification/tx/vault/LeanVaultDeposit_test.cpp#L466)). The withdraw payout is the symmetric case.

Thanks to @hmalinski for finding the large-totals edge case and proposing the exact integer approach, the new gate, the share truncation, and the zero-payout check.

### API Impact

- [ ] Public API: New feature (new methods and/or new fields)
- [ ] Public API: Breaking change (in general, breaking changes should only impact the next api_version)
- [x] `libxrpl` change: `assetsToSharesDeposit`, `sharesToAssetsDeposit`, `assetsToSharesWithdraw` and `sharesToAssetsWithdraw` in `include/xrpl/ledger/helpers/VaultHelpers.h` each gain a defaulted `VaultRounding` parameter (source-compatible; the default preserves prior behavior).
- [ ] Peer protocol change (must be backward compatible or bump the peer protocol version)

## Before / After

Pool of 100 assets and 3 shares (MPT):

| Operation | Fair value | Before | After (`fixCleanup3_6_0`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Deposit 34, mints 1 share | 33.33 | charged 33 | charged 34 |
| Withdraw 2 shares | 66.67 | paid 67 | paid 66 |
| Withdraw 50 assets without `fixCleanup3_4_0` | | burns 2 shares, pays 67 | burns 1 share, pays 33 |

Exact rates, and cases where round-to-nearest already rounds the safe way, are unchanged.

## Test Plan

The test scenarios for the large-totals edge case, the zero-payout rejection and the `fixCleanup3_6_0` gating come from @hmalinski, who found the edge case and described these tests in #7824.

- `VaultRounding_test` (new): transaction-level tests on CashBasis and FixedPrecision MPT vaults, each with and without `fixCleanup3_6_0`: the deposit and withdraw dilution cases (by shares and by amount), the large-totals deposit and withdrawal, the zero-payout rejection on both withdraw branches (and with `fixCleanup3_4_0` off), and share truncation without `fixCleanup3_4_0`.
- `VaultHelpers_test`: helper-level tests for MPT and XRP, including the large-totals case and a check that `FavorVault` leaves IOU conversions unchanged.
- `VaultBugs_test` and `LoanRounding_test`: two pre-`fixCleanup3_4_0` bug repros now also disable `fixCleanup3_6_0`, which fixes them on its own; each gains a run showing that.

Local run (Release, asserts on): all `Vault*` suites, `xrpl.tx.Loan*`, `xrpl.app.LoanBroker*` and `xrpl.app.Invariants*` pass (38 suites, 186,832 tests, 0 failures).

### 🔵 Needs a closer look Consensus-critical vault accounting changes across amendment combinations and lending interactions warrant independent domain review and transaction-level validation of impaired-loan and transfer-fee cases. **No open issues** 🎉
What changed in this PR This PR prevents shareholder dilution in XRP and MPT vaults by using exact integer conversions rounded in the vault’s favor under `fixCleanup3_6_0`. Legacy conversion behavior remains the default, and IOU conversion arithmetic and clawback behavior are unchanged. **Changes:** - Add exact 128-bit conversions that floor share counts and withdrawal payouts, while rounding deposit charges up. - Apply amendment-gated rounding to deposits and withdrawals, align withdrawal-limit estimates, and reject non-final zero-value payouts. - Add regression coverage for dilution, large totals, zero payouts, and amendment combinations. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `src/​test/​app/​vault/​VaultRounding_test.cpp` | Add transaction-level rounding and amendment-gating tests for both vault versions. | | `src/​test/​app/​vault/​VaultHelpers_test.cpp` | Test exact XRP/MPT conversions and unchanged IOU arithmetic. | | `src/​test/​app/​vault/​VaultBugs_test.cpp` | Update overshoot regression tests for the new amendment. | | `src/​test/​app/​lending/​LoanRounding_test.cpp` | Cover zero-payout rejection with different amendment combinations. | | `src/​libxrpl/​tx/​transactors/​vault/​VaultWithdraw.cpp` | Apply rounding, truncate shares, and guard against zero payouts. | | `src/​libxrpl/​tx/​transactors/​vault/​VaultDeposit.cpp` | Enable vault-favoring deposit conversions behind the amendment. | | `src/​libxrpl/​ledger/​helpers/​VaultHelpers.cpp` | Implement exact integer multiply-divide conversions with directed rounding. | | `include/​xrpl/​ledger/​helpers/​VaultHelpers.h` | Declare and document the defaulted `VaultRounding` parameters. |

reviews.author: hmalinski
reviews.body:
Thanks for picking this back up. The exact integer path, the gate and the zero-payout check all look right to me. I also checked that the rounded-up deposit charge can never exceed the amount offered: the share count is floored from the amount, so the ceiling of its value is at most the amount. Two things:

**1. Clawback still rounds to nearest.**
`VaultClawback.cpp:307`, `:327` and `:349` still use the legacy conversion. The description notes this, and it leaves the same dilution in place.

Example: a vault holds 100 units with 3 shares outstanding. Clawing back 67 from a holder with 2 shares burns both shares and recovers 67, although they were worth 66⅔. The remaining share drops from 33⅓ to 33. The 3_4_0 truncation bounds recovery by the requested amount, and the `AssetsAvailable` clamp bounds it by what's available, but neither bounds it by fair value.

Changing just those three calls to `FavorVault` isn't quite enough. A recovery that floors to zero would burn shares without moving the vault balance, and the clawback invariant rejects that for a non-empty vault (`VaultInvariant.cpp:1445-1449`). So it needs explicit zero-recovery handling, like the new withdraw guard. I'm fine with it as a follow-up under the same amendment, or a sentence in the description on why it's out of scope. It would be nice to settle before 3_6_0 ships, so it doesn't need another amendment later.

**2. Helper tests with nonzero unrealized loss.**
Every `FavorVault` helper case uses `makeVaultAndIssuance`, which sets `sfLossUnrealized` to 0 (`VaultHelpers_test.cpp:603`), and `WaiveUnrealizedLoss::No`. Both withdraw helpers feed `AssetsTotal − LossUnrealized` into the integer path, so it has to be a whole number. Could you add XRP/MPT helper cases with `LossUnrealized > 0`, a non-zero payout, and both `WaiveUnrealizedLoss` values? `LoanRounding_test` already covers the impaired zero-payout and fully-impaired cases through the transactors, so those don't need repeating.

FYI: #8358 changes these helpers to take `VaultEntryR const&`, which needs a view to construct. Whichever PR lands second will need a small rebase, including the helper tests that pass raw SLEs.

Happy to approve once item 2 is in and item 1 is either handled or noted as a follow-up.

Adding a separate PR just to add the amendment makes it easier to manage separate/independent PRs that may require the amendment.
